newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-LINESMAN THREATENED AFTER PENALTY CONTROVERSY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LINESMAN THREATENED AFTER PENALTY CONTROVERSY.

text.p: The linesman behind a hotly- debated penalty decision that put Barcelona on the way to victory at the weekend has had his life turned upside down in a real-life re-run of a Spanish film farce.

Rafael Guerrero has received telephone threats and seen the school where he works as a caretaker daubed with grafitti after telling referee Enrique Mejuto of an alleged infringement in Zaragoza's game with Barcelona.
On his advice, Mejuto sent off Zaragoza's Xavier Aguado and awarded the penalty from which Barcelona equalised.
Barcelona went on to win 5-3 in the final minutes after trailing 3-1.
But television replays suggest that Guerrero was probably mistaken about the player involved, and possibly the nature of the incident.
Television viewers have been treated to unexpurgated versions -- complete with heavy obscentities -- of the conversation in which Guerrero explained the incident to Mejuto.
Mejuto asks the linesman what he is signalling for and Guerrero replies: "penalty and sending off."
Mejuto then utters the description of an obscene act.

A television microphone clearly captured the conversation in detail and on Monday evening supporters at Atletico Madrid's game with Hercules were already chanting the best-known and most obscene phrases of the exchange uttered by the referee to the linesman. The phrases look likely to enter modern folk vocabulary.
Meanwhile, and to nobody's surprise, outspoken Atletico president Jesus Gil jumped into the controversy with his own interpretation.

"Barcelona, as always, ended up as the beneficiary...it would have been more complicated if the referee had made the same decision in the other area," said Gil, who recognised that Mejuto was one of the best officials in the Spanish league.

Guerrero's problems echo those of a recent film comedy 'Matias the linesman', in which a linesman who calls a penalty against the Spanish national side has to take refuge from angry fans in a remote village.
